en.title: Implement a FIFO Queue Using Two Stacks
en.description:
The queue starts empty. Implement push, pop, peek, and empty using only two stacks. Output the return value of every operation, with null for push; this site does not output anything for the constructor. The judge checks behavior only, so please respect the two-stack restriction in your implementation.

This site independently wrote the standard I/O, examples, solution, and tests.
en.input: The first line contains the number of operations Q (1..100), followed by Q lines: push x (1..9), pop, peek, or empty. The queue is guaranteed to be non-empty for pop and peek.
en.output: Output the Q return values on one line, separated by spaces, using null, true, false, or integers.
en.explanation:
Example 1: the return values are null, null, 1, 1, false in order, and 2 remains in the queue at the end.

Example 2: the queue starts empty, so it returns true.

Example 3: 9 is enqueued and then removed, leaving the queue empty; the return values are null, 9, true.
hints: The input stack holds new elements. When the output stack is empty, pour the entire input stack into it; pop and peek operate on the top of the output stack.
